chunks: Aban narrated from Abu al-Jarud who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'A man does not buy back what he has given in charity. And if he gives a house as charity to a relative, if he wishes, he may live with them. And if he gives a servant as charity to a relative, if he wishes, the servant may serve him.'
ai.seo_question: Can a donor buy back a house or servant they gave as charity to a relative?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that while a donor generally cannot repurchase their own charity, gifts given to relatives allow the donor to retain usufruct rights, such as residing in the property or utilizing the servant, if they choose. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Sadaqah* to relatives, balancing the finality of the gift with familial care and practical utility.
